vo: Myth: a passing test report means you're certified.
A certificate has to list each applicable rule, separately.
It also names the product, certifier, and test date and place.
The test supports the certificate. It isn't the certificate.

caption:
Passing test report? That's not the same as a finished certificate.
A finished product certificate has its own required content: each applicable rule listed separately, the product, the certifier, a records contact, and when and where it was made and tested.
The test supports the certificate. It isn't the certificate.

sources.claim: Certificate must identify applicable rules separately
sources.quote: (2) State each consumer product safety rule under the CPSA, or similar rule, ban, standard, or regulation under any law enforced by the Commission, to which the finished product(s) are being certified. Finished product certificates must identify separately all applicable rules, bans, standards, or regulations.
(1) Identify the finished product(s) covered by the certificate.
(3) Identify the finished product certifier that is certifying compliance of the finished product(s), as set forth in § 1110.7

(4) Identify and provide contact information (consisting, at a minimum, of the individual's name, street address, city, state or province, country or administrative region, email address, and telephone number) for the individual maintaining records listed in § 1110.17 on behalf of the finished product certifier.

sources.claim: Certificate gives date and place of manufacture
sources.quote: (5) Provide the date (month and year, at a minimum) and place (including a manufacturer name, ...) where the finished product(s) were manufactured, produced, or assembled.

sources.claim: Certificate gives most recent test date and place (not results)
sources.quote: (6) Provide the most recent date and place(s) (...) where the finished product(s) were tested for compliance with the rule(s), ban(s), standard(s), or regulation(s)
